subject: Re: Brookline Health demo scheduling — DST-aware window?
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@brooklinehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-24T09:15:00-04:00
Subject: Quick demo — can your EU engineers join early ET?

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick reply on our intake form. We’re a small IT team at Brookline Health and would like a short walkthrough of Redwood’s private deployment options (30–40 minutes). Our primary stakeholders are East Coast — best windows for us are 08:30–10:00 ET or 19:00–20:30 ET.

We noticed your team is in Europe and are concerned about daylight savings this week — would EU engineers be available at those times? If not, could you propose an alternate?

We prefer a live Q&A and would like at least one engineer on the call who can speak to VPC/networking.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of IT, Brookline Health
attachments: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: Brookline Health Scheduling <scheduling@brooklinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-24T16:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Quick demo — can your EU engineers join early ET?

Hi Samantha — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the windows. We can do both, but there are DST flips this weekend across regions and that will change who is on-duty: EU clocks move back one hour on Sunday night (local) which temporarily shifts our morning/late-evening alignment.

Two pragmatic options that work for us and meet your ask for VPC/networking coverage:

- Option A (best for your 08:30–10:00 ET): Schedule a 09:00 ET slot on Tue/Wed next week. That will be 14:00–15:30 CET and we’ll have our EU networking engineer live.
- Option B (best for your 19:00–20:30 ET): Rotate hosts across two sessions — Redwood EU leads the first session (19:00 ET = 00:00 CET during DST week, which is painful) but we can instead propose 20:00 ET on Thu which becomes 01:00 CET if we must, OR we can flip to Redwood US engineers for late-evening ET slots if you prefer slightly different availability.

If you’re flexible with a 30–45 minute slot, we recommend Option A (morning ET) or an alternating schedule where we record one session and run a live follow-up.

I attached a short agenda and a calendar invite stub. Can you confirm: preferred date(s) and whether you want the recording copy?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: brookline-demo-agenda.pdf, brookline-demo-invite.ics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T08:45:00+01:00
Subject: RE: Brookline scheduling — DST/host rotation thought (internal)

Mina — quick internal note before we lock on dates. Europe rolls clocks back on Sun (25th local), so our CET offsets will shift. Practical points:

- If we promise a 14:00 CET slot next Tue, that’s stable — team will be on normal hours.
- If Brookline insists on a 19:00 ET start this week (before Friday), that maps to 00:00+ CET during the DST overlap — we should avoid asking EU folks to take that shift.
- Suggestion: offer them two options in the reply: Tue 09:00 ET (EU on standard hours) or Thu 14:00 ET (US-led late afternoon but with US engineer). If they prefer evening ET consistently, we can rotate hosts (EU handles mornings ET, US handles evening ET) and note the rotation in the invite.

Also — flag the recording + follow-up office hours as the compromise. Rishi, can you confirm US engineer availability Thu 20:00 ET? If yes I’ll add them to the invite.

Jonas
Lead SRE, Redwood Inference
(Internal)

Subject: Re: Quick demo — confirmed slot and recording option

Thanks for the quick replies. Based on team availability and the DST change we’ll keep this simple:

Confirmed slot (pick one):
- Tue 2026-11-02 at 09:00 ET / 14:00 CET — 35 minutes, live with EU networking engineer (recommended)
- Thu 2026-11-04 at 20:00 ET / 01:00 CET (next day) — 35 minutes, live with US networking engineer (if you need an evening ET option)

If you’d like both, we can run the Tue session live and the Thu session as a shorter follow-up with Q&A, and we’ll share a recording of the first session.

Practical notes:
- We won’t ask EU engineers to do midnight shifts — if you take the evening ET option we’ll have our US engineer lead.
- Recording will be available within 24 hours of the session; we can redact any sensitive slides on request.

Please confirm which slot you prefer and whether we should add a separate follow-up Q&A slot. I’ve reattached the agenda and a calendar invite (placeholder).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
